record.original_question: Derive incompleteness results for determining quantum algorithmic information.

evidence.quote: 17. Derive incompleteness results for the determination of quantum algorithmic information. (K. Svozil)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a universal (prefix-free) classical Turing machine $U$, the algorithmic (Kolmogorov–Chaitin) information content of a finite binary string $x$ is $K(x)=\min\{|p|:U(p)=x\}$, and the halting probability is $\Omega_U=\sum_{p:\,U(p)\downarrow}2^{-|p|}$. Classical algorithmic information theory yields incompleteness results of Chaitin type: for any recursively axiomatizable, sound formal system $T$ there is a constant $c_T$ such that $T$ cannot prove any true statement of the form "$K(x)>c_T$"; equivalently, only finitely many bits of $\Omega_U$ are provable in $T$.

Now let $\mathcal H$ be a separable Hilbert space and let a universal quantum Turing machine $\mathcal Q$ be fixed. For a quantum state $|\psi\rangle\in\mathcal H$ (or, more generally, for a finite description of a quantum object such as a unitary, a measurement outcome, or a qubit string), define a notion of quantum algorithmic information $K_{\mathcal Q}(|\psi\rangle)$ as the infimum, up to a prescribed fidelity $\varepsilon>0$, of the lengths of quantum programs $|p\rangle$ such that $\mathcal Q$ on input $|p\rangle$ outputs a state $\varepsilon$-close (in trace distance) to $|\psi\rangle$. Analogously, define a quantum halting probability $\Omega_{\mathcal Q}$ associated with $\mathcal Q$.

Problem. Establish Chaitin-style incompleteness theorems for the determination of quantum algorithmic information. Concretely, prove (or disprove) the following, and identify the precise constants and resources involved:

(a) For every recursively axiomatizable, sound formal system $T$ (in a language capable of formalizing quantum Turing machines and rational approximations to amplitudes), there exists a constant $c_T<\infty$ such that for no specific quantum description $|\psi\rangle$ can $T$ prove the statement "$K_{\mathcal Q}(|\psi\rangle)>c_T$" (at the fixed fidelity $\varepsilon$).

(b) The binary expansion of $\Omega_{\mathcal Q}$ is algorithmically random, and any sound recursively axiomatizable $T$ can determine only finitely many of its bits.

(c) Identify the analogue of the Berry/Chaitin paradox in the quantum setting and quantify how access to qubits (entanglement, superposition, or oracle access to quantum randomness) modifies the provability bound $c_T$ relative to the classical Kolmogorov complexity case.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of deriving Chaitin-style incompleteness theorems specifically for quantum algorithmic information appears to remain open as posed. Related partial results exist: Svozil and collaborators have developed quantum algorithmic information theory and shown that many classical features (machine-independence, complexity bounds) carry over, and Calude–Svozil and others have proved incomputability of quantum randomness with experimental tests. Recent work (e.g., Goldbring et al., 2024) establishes undecidability and incompleteness phenomena in quantum information theory and operator algebras, but a full Chaitin-style incompleteness theorem for quantum Kolmogorov complexity and a quantum halting probability $\Omega_{\mathcal Q}$ does not appear to be definitively established.

status_evidence.title: Quantum algorithmic information theory (Svozil)
status_evidence.snippet: Features and results of classical algorithmic information theory hold for quantum algorithmic information as well; universal quantum computers have machine-independent quantum algorithmic information content.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational framework exists but explicit incompleteness theorems for quantum AIT are not stated as solved.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Randomness, Quantum Physics, and Incompleteness
status_evidence.snippet: Explores relations between Heisenberg uncertainty and Gödel incompleteness via algorithmic complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Connection between quantum physics and incompleteness explored but Chaitin-style theorems for quantum AIT not derived.

status_evidence.title: Undecidability and incompleteness in quantum information theory and operator algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) survey of undecidability/incompleteness in quantum information theory.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses related undecidability phenomena, indicating the area is active.

status_evidence.title: Experimental Evidence of Quantum Randomness Incomputability
status_evidence.snippet: Calude–Svozil show quantum randomness is provably incomputable, with experimental tests.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result on incomputability, but not full incompleteness theorem for quantum K-complexity.
